recipes.name: Savory Venison Meatloaf
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) packet saltine crackers, finely crushed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix together venison, onion, 1/4 cup barbecue sauce, egg, crushed crackers, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, sage, and steak seasoning in a large bowl with your hands until evenly combined. Pack into a 3x7-inch loaf pan. Lay bacon slices over the top.

Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center and bacon is crispy, about 35 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

Meanwhile, stir together remaining 3/4 cup barbecue sauce, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce in a small saucepan over medium heat. Simmer for 5 minutes, whisking constantly, until sauce is heated through and slightly thickened.
Pour sauce over cooked meatloaf and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Savory Venison Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: This venison meatloaf wrapped in bacon features onion and crushed saltines and is topped with a barbecue sauce made with brown sugar and Worcestershire.

review.reviewBody: Made this meatloaf last night after having made the same recipe for years (20+ actually) and I think we have found our new favorite meatloaf recipe! I substituted store-bought bbq sauce for some home made that I whipped together!

I am an avid deer hunter and the recipe by itself is amazing. But like all recipes there is absolutely nothing wrong with tweaking a bit. I follow the recipe with a few adjustments and additions. Again this is just my take but everyone raves aboit it. 1 tsp of sage instead of 1/2, 1 medium to large white onion instead of 1/2 a yellow onion, 2 garlic cloves finely chopped, 1 cup of shredded cheese (I use Mexican four blend), and HEB Speciality Series Texas BBQ sauce (gotta have that Texas kick). I then top it with 4 thick slices of maple bacon. Try it out. You will not be disappointed.
I made this dish and it was really good but as a suggestion, do not add brown sugar to the glaze...bbq sauce already has it in there and it was too sweet for my taste.

I had never cooked with venison before and was a little nervous, but this recipe turned out great! My husband said it was the best he had ever tasted. I did add 1/2 lb of 90% ground beef to the venison as well, and did 1/2 BBQ sauce and 1/2 ketchup wherever it called for BBQ sauce, but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. Mine seemed to take longer to cook- about 45 min or an hour, then 5 min on broil to crisp up the bacon, but that could be because I'm at high altitude. Give this one a try!

This was an excellent way to cook venison. When a family member shoots a deer there is a lot of meat to use and this will be a keeper. I doubled the main recipe but not the sauce and then served the sauce on the side rather than slathered on top.

I have never made anything with venison and I decided to make this meatloaf because a friend gave me a pound of fresh venison along with a pound of fresh ground beef, I used half a pound of venison and half a pound of ground beef and instead of the BBQ sauce called for I used Sweet Baby Rays Vidalia Onion along with 1 tablespoon of Honey (when it came to topping it with 3/4 cup of BBQ sauce I used 1 1/2 tablespoons of honey with the BBQ sauce no substitute on brown sugar) and it is absolutely fabulous! Thank you so much for this recipe! My reason for the substitution was because I already had this BBQ sauce.

Made this last night, just amazing. I did tweak a couple minor details. I used Italian bread crumbs instead of crackers, added a chopped jalapeño, added a 1/2 lb of cooked breakfast sausage to mix in the meat for fat content (did not take away any of the deer taste, couldn't hardly tell sausage was present)... next time I plan on adding shredded cheddar cheese just because.

Turned out savory indeed and I will keep this recipe (in fact I'm re-making 2 of these meatloaves as we speak). However, my baking time was significantly longer than 35 minutes, closer to twice that time. I would recommend to use a food thermometer to ensure properly cooked meat until/unless you know your oven.

Absolutely delicious! I didn’t have steak seasoning so I used 3/8th tsp of adobo and 1/8 tsp of onion powder instead because the ingredients were similar to steak seasoning I googled. So tender and juicy. My husband loved it!

Fantastic! I have made this 5 times now and every time I get positive feedback from anyone that tries it. The only changes I made were oatmeal instead of crackers, didn't add bacon and doubled the recipe. I also have never made the extra sauce for on top. It is so incredibly moist even without it.
I added in chopped bacon to the mix and still added the bacon on top. This came out perfect. Everyone who ate it loved it even the person who was hesitant about meatloaf.
Great use for venison burger - excellent meatloaf, the bacon totally makes it. Hubby loved it! Will make this again
Made this twice now. First time was venison, and just made it tonight with antelope. The family devoured it both times. No leftovers for me! :-(

This was absolutely THE BEST use of our ground venison. Hubby loves it and i love it, too. I used a spicier BBQ sauce and only had about 1/3 of a cup left for the top layer. It was perfect. It doesn't really need much sauce of the top, especially if you use ketchup on your meatloaf. This is a keeper recipe, for sure!
Very moist. Exceptional taste.
Makes great meatloaf sandwiches
I have made this using venison, bear, elk, beef and ground turkey. It is awesome in every format.

I was pleasantly surprised this recipe and even more surprised that even my picky kids loved it! This recipe is a keeper!! The only thing I changed is for the sauce on top I used mostly ketchup with about 1/4 cup of bbq sauce just to make sure it wasn’t too spicy!

Hate meatloaf; always have. This recipe is SOOOOOOO freaking delicious!! I'm a convert, and my very picky kids are as well. It's SO good that I even make it for company. Yep, you read that right! Company meatloaf!!!! Nineteen stars!! (Oh, and I've never written a review here before!)
will definitely make this again
